observations: The local Terra CLI queue worker exited after a transient SSH listing failure. Pending GPU cases continued waiting and some timed out. The worker was restarted; queue listing failures now retry without terminating the consumer.

For BCSS cohesive boundary expansion, cases 014, 017 and 018 passed cell-count checks but selected an entire tumor-component population zone. The reference-shape gate then rejected the component-local provenance, whereas validated cases used interface-band or certified changed-tissue zones.
software_changes: SSH/SCP list and transfer operations retry transient failures. A successfully completed Terra decision is retained during response-upload retries, so the model is not called again for a transport-only upload failure. The transfer version is committed but will apply to the long-running consumer only after a safe restart.

The joint Planner now receives an explicit cohesive-boundary core-zone constraint and rejects a whole-component zone before expensive execution. This does not choose the interface for the LLM or loosen any final gate.
audit_rule: Classify CLI transport and wall-clock failures separately. Preserve every initial attempt; rerun only the same frozen case with an explicit attempt link. A process uses the code it imported at its own start time.
verification: Four local queue tests passed. Two server-side joint Planner tests passed, including a regression that rejects whole-component zones for cohesive boundary expansion.
